title: Noise-Robust Factoring
statement: Nontrivial-factor recovery from noisy quantum samples using the classical postprocessing of Theorem 4.5.

target.description: Odd composite input under the short-vector and well-spread sample-noise hypotheses.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.meaning: Number of samples divided by dimension

parameters.name: p
parameters.meaning: Probability that a sample is corrupted

assumptions: Conjecture 3.1 on a short vector in $L\setminus L_0$.
Section 4.2.1's independent sample-corruption model, specialized here to uniform additive noise; not arbitrary adversarial noise.
All constraints of Lemma 4.4 and the Gaussian-radius bound following Theorem 4.5 are required.

time.note: No total bound is extracted for this coordinate in the checked result.

memory.note: No total classical/quantum memory bound is extracted for this result.

classical_time.note: Theorem 4.5 classical postprocessing from the specified sample batch.

quantum_calls.note: One source sample per call; this is a sample budget, not total runtime.

success.description: Theorem 4.5 guarantee over the prescribed sample and error distribution, under Conjecture 3.1 and Lemma 4.4's parameter constraints.

review.scope: Checked the stated event and bound in the cited theorem/corollary and its surrounding argument; not a proof reproduction.

evidence.locator: PDF pp. 17–19 / printed pp. 14–16, Section 4.2, Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 4.5.
evidence.interpretation: Targeted transcription of this result's input, output, cost accounting and success event; not a full-paper audit.

limitations: The standalone space-efficient exponentiation and circuit-only optimizations are not separate active analyses.
The admissible error rate and A constraint belong to this parameter choice; they are not interchangeable independent minima.
